articles.title: Belgian cyclist hit by driver while training, out of road world championships in Montreal
articles.summary: Belgian cyclist Seff Van Kerckhove was transported to hospital after he was hit by a driver during a training ride just outside Montreal on Sunday afternoon, according to the Belgian cycling…

image.caption: Belgian Seff Van Kerckhove was slated to compete in the men's junior time trial race in Montreal on Tuesday. (Dirk Waem/Belga Mag/AFP via Getty Images)

blocks.text: Montreal·Updated

Belgian cyclist Seff Van Kerckhove was transported to hospital after he was hit by a driver during a training ride just outside Montreal on Sunday afternoon, according to the Belgian cycling federation.
Seff Van Kerckhove, 18, slated to compete in 2 races this week, will not be replaced, says cycling federation

The incident left the 18-year-old unable to participate in the UCI Road World Championships happening this week in Montreal. He was slated to compete in the men's junior individual time trial on Tuesday and in the road race on Thursday.
"The collision had a severe impact on his upper body," said a spokesperson for Belgian Cycling, Gwendoline Gerres, in a news release.
She said he is already undergoing rehab.
"We wish him a speedy recovery."
The federation adds it will not replace Van Kerckhove in either of the races he was scheduled to participate in.

This is the second collision the teenager has had with a car in just the last nine months. A crash in Belgium in December left Van Kerckhove with four fractured vertebrae, and he only returned to training in April.
He was a podium hopeful this week in Montreal after finishing third last year in the world junior men's time trial in Rwanda.
Van Kerckhove's brother Matisse, who's also competing in Montreal in the U23 time trial, spoke to a Belgian newspaper about the incident.

"From what I understand, a car suddenly drove across the street, presumably to turn onto a driveway," the brother told Het Laatste Nieuws. "The driver of that car didn’t see Seff coming, and because Seff was in his time trial handlebars at that moment, he couldn’t brake in time and crashed head-on into that car.”

items: Professional cyclists can top 100 km/h. But safety has not kept pace — and people are dying

blocks.text: According to Montreal police, the incident happened outside its territory, in a Montreal suburb, though they couldn't say where exactly.

In a statement, the local organizing race committee said every national federation is responsible for choosing where to accommodate its team and deciding on the training course. It says that while some are staying in Montreal, others are off-island.

articles.title: First UK charges brought over 1994 Rwanda genocide
articles.summary: Dr Vincent Brown, formerly Dr Vincent Bajinya, 65, will appear at Westminster Magistrates’ Court on Tuesday charged with seven offences.

blocks.text: A Rwandan man, who has been living in north London, has been charged with offences relating to the 1994 genocide in Rwanda.
The Crown Prosecution Service said it was the first time charges relating to the genocide against the Tutsi in Rwanda have been brought in the UK.
Dr Vincent Brown, formerly Dr Vincent Bajinya, 65, has been charged with one offence of conduct ancillary to genocide and six offences of conduct ancillary to murder as a crime against humanity.
He will appear at Westminster Magistrates' Court on Tuesday.

articles.title: Aeta community in Capas, Tarlac in limbo over Pax Silica hub
articles.summary: Petronila Muñoz walked across the sweeping grasslands she has called home for generations, uncertain about its future, as a sprawling tech hub for the Pax Silica initiative takes shape.
articles.byline: PAM CASTRO and CHAD WILLIAMS, Agence France-Presse

blocks.text: CAPAS, Tarlac — Tribal leader Petronila Muñoz walked across the sweeping grasslands she has called home for generations, uncertain about its future, as a sprawling tech hub for the US-led Pax Silica initiative takes shape.

With little information and no prior consultation, the Indigenous chieftain said her Aeta Hungey tribe was uncertain how much of their land could be affected or what will become of the livelihood it provides.
"There's still no clarity," Muñoz told AFP inside the tribe's traditional meeting hall.
"What will happen to us? That's our biggest question."

In April, the United States announced that the Philippines had joined Pax Silica, a US-led effort to strengthen supply chains for semiconductors and rare earth elements and reduce participating countries' dependence on China.

The Philippines has designated a 1,620-hectare (4,000-acre) site in New Clark City in Tarlac province, north of Manila, for a manufacturing hub aimed at producing high-end components for use in artificial intelligence data centers.
The government estimates the initiative could attract up to $70 billion in investment and create about 190,000 jobs, a major boost to a country with more than three million unemployed people.
The project has a long timeline. No tenants have been confirmed.
Plans to domestically process the country's mineral resources could be even further away.
For about 1,000 Aetas, however, the prospect of displacement is already here.
In July, they received a letter from the Bases Conversion and Development Authority (BCDA) warning that the project "could affect your occupied lands."
EXPLAINER: What is Pax Silica and why are people worried?
'Money runs out'

Muñoz said visiting BCDA employees told them to leave by December and relocate to an area about 16 kilometers (10 miles) from their current home, without providing a master plan showing which parts of their ancestral domains would be affected.
Muñoz said the BCDA has offered them just P30 per square meter for their lands, an offer all declined.
"Our lives, our livelihood and our culture are tied to this ancestral land," Muñoz said.
"Land is more important. Money runs out."

blocks.caption: Aeta tribal chieftain Petronila Muñozs holds a draft of the land historical claims in Capas, Tarlac province on September 2, 2026. Jam Sta. Rosa/ AFP

blocks.text: Aeta tribal chieftain Petronila Muñozs holds a draft of the land historical claims in Capas, Tarlac province on September 2, 2026. Jam Sta. Rosa/ AFP
The BCDA declined to address specific questions about the Aetas' situation and rejected a freedom of information request for the site's official boundary map and geospatial data.
It said the information was being "withheld temporarily until the official action is finalized or published."
At a Senate hearing last month, BCDA president Joshua Bingcang said the Aetas were living on government land. Like many Indigenous groups in the Philippines, they hold no land title.
Civic groups have also raised concerns about the project's environmental impact, particularly the demand for water and electricity in a country plagued by droughts and rotational power outages.
The US State Department told AFP that "environmental, water, energy, and community-impact studies" would inform the project's design.
"Before any major development happens, we expect rigorous stakeholder impact assessments will take place," a spokesperson said.
Bingcang told the Senate that investors would be required to build their own power and water systems.
'We have to open up'

Alvin Camba, research director at an AI firm focused on supply chains and risk assessment, said Manila's close relationship with the United States could motivate investors to set up shop despite the power concerns.
Last month, reports said Washington planned to warn countries they could be excluded from Pax Silica if they joined a rival framework backed by Beijing.

"This is where the advantage of the Philippines comes in. The Philippines is the least affected by Chinese capital in Southeast Asia," Camba told AFP, saying the country would offer foreign companies the ability to "disentangle" from China.
For political economist Calixto Chikiamco, Pax Silica represents a "historic opportunity" for the Philippines to move beyond its traditional wheelhouse of microchip testing and packaging.
"We have to open up to foreign investment so that technology transfer [to the Philippines] will happen," he told AFP.
Sacrifices
The BCDA has been conducting public consultations in Tarlac and nearby provinces, but the agency has yet to hold talks with her tribe, Muñoz said.
The Aetas remain uncertain if the government would help them build new homes or provide land to cultivate for income if they are moved.
"I wish they would listen to us. They're just talking among themselves," she said, adding she worried her tribe would not be qualified for the sort of new jobs Pax Silica promised.
While a proponent of the initiative, Chikiamco said the government was doing "a terrible job" explaining the benefits and tradeoffs it represented.
Camba agreed: "I would actually advise the Philippine government to be very transparent about what's happening. A big problem is transparency."
Still, the benefits outweigh the risks, he said.
"Every country that has... jump-started development has had to make sacrifices," Camba said.
But 63-year-old Muñoz, who hopes to be buried in her tribe's traditional burial ground, said she would not leave, even if a backhoe flattened her home.
"Why do we have to be the ones to sacrifice for the kind of development they want?" she asked. — AFP

articles.title: U.S. strikes on boats alleged to be carrying drugs may be 'crimes against humanity,' UN expert says
articles.summary: A United Nations special rapporteur has published a damning report on the U.S. military campaign of missile strikes on boats allegedly transporting drugs, characterizing them as "serial extrajudicial…

image.caption: A combination image shows two screengrabs from a video posted on the X account of the White House on Sept. 15, 2025. The U.S. government campaign on alleged drug-carrying boats is now past the one-year mark, with international law experts condemning the attacks. (The White House/Reuters)

blocks.text: A United Nations special rapporteur has published a damning report on the U.S. military campaign of missile strikes on boats allegedly transporting drugs, characterizing them as "serial extrajudicial killings."

Ben Saul, chair of international law at the University of Sydney, concluded his report on the attacks on boats in the Caribbean Sea and Pacific Ocean before the most recent of incidents. The U.S. military attacked a boat it suspected of being used to smuggle drugs in the Caribbean Sea on Saturday, killing four people to bring the overall total of dead in the campaign to at least 231 people across 69 strikes since September 2025.

U.S. President Donald Trump's administration has said it has the right to self-defence in what it calls an armed conflict with narco-terrorists. Last year, the White House invoked the centuries-old Alien Enemies Act to proclaim that Venezuelan gang Tren de Aragua is engaged in an "invasion" and "irregular warfare" against the U.S. through its transport of drugs.

The administration sought to connect Tren de Aragua's drug operations to the Nicolás Maduro government. However, the strikes on boats have continued even after the U.S. military seized Maduro in a January operation and embarked on a working relationship with a former member of his government, interim President Delcy Rodriguez.

items: Canada restricts drug boat intel from U.S. navy's Caribbean airstrike operation

blocks.text: In his report, Saul wrote that the U.S. attacks are unjustifiable under a wide range of criteria, ranging from international humanitarian law, international law of the sea, international counterterrorism law, narcotics suppression conventions and notions of national or personal self-defence.
"The United States military attacks are … contrary to international law, violate the human right to life and plausibly constitute crimes against humanity," said Saul.
Independent experts appointed by the UN Human Rights Council have also previously condemned the attacks.
3 Ecuadorian boats unaccounted for

The American claims of self-defence fail on a number of grounds, Saul said, with the U.S. never presenting evidence of the threat of an armed attack from any of the boats, making the military's attacks disproportionate.
The U.S. hasn't established that the Venezuelan government has sent the boats, according to Saul, and even if they had, "drug trafficking is not equivalent to the military attack," he wrote.
Most drug use does not result in death or immediate serious injury, the UN rapporteur said, and there can be a series of intervening activities in the supply chain before a user consumes drugs.
"There are reasonable grounds to believe that the reported 68 attacks that killed 223 people constituted crimes against humanity of murder under customary international law," said Saul.
"Murder means the unlawful killing of a person where the perpetrator intended to cause death or knew that it would occur in the ordinary course of events."
CBC speaks to a former adviser to the U.S. Department of State on the strikes on alleged drug boats
Saul also raised concerns in his report about three more vessels that have "sunk in suspicious circumstances without any claim of responsibility."

The list includes the Ecuadorian boat Fiorella, whose eight to 10 crew members disappeared at sea in January. The crew reported being surveilled, and relatives of the men aboard say the Fiorella was a fishing vessel.

Gloria Alexandra Bravo Cedeño, the prosecutor in Ecuador tasked with investigating what happened to the three vessels, was fatally shot in June. No arrests have been made in connection with her killing.
Criteria for striking boats classified

At a July committee hearing, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said a wide range of intelligence from multiple sources is assessed before the strikes — which have been carried out by drones and fighter jets — take place.

"Every strike has a legal officer on the deck that has to make a determination whether the call is legal or not, and this is done by the Department of War — the way it has been done in other theatres around the world," said Rubio.
"I can tell you they do walk away from strikes," he said at another point.
U.S. authorization of 2nd strike of Venezuelan ship questioned

The U.S. Defence Department, renamed the Department of War by the Trump administration, is using three criteria to determine whether to strike, U.S. senators have said. What they are remains the subject of classified briefings.

Democratic Sen. Tim Kaine, of Virginia, while not divulging the classified material, expressed wonder at the July hearing that the the presence of narcotics on a boat is not among those targeting criteria.

Sen. Rand Paul, arguably the foremost Republican critic of the strikes, added that the presence of arms also is not among the criteria. Paul, from Kentucky, expressed concerns about the campaign, given the precedent in drug interdiction efforts.
"The statistics from the [U.S.] Coast Guard say that when we interdict alleged drug boats in the historic way, the way we've always done it, about one in four don't have drugs," said Paul.
"We make mistakes. We see something suspicious about the boat, we stop them and they don't have drugs on board."

items: These Trinidadian fishermen were killed in a U.S. boat strike. Now their families are suing
U.S. sending survivors of strike on alleged 'drug-carrying submarine' back to South America, Trump says

blocks.text: Lawmakers from both parties were particularly alarmed by reports from a Sept. 2, 2025, strike that killed two people who had climbed on top of part of a boat that had been partially destroyed in an initial attack.
That incident, Saul wrote, is "in violation of the right to life and the duty to rescue at sea."
Traffickers may be adapting to campaign

As with other strikes, the U.S. military on Saturday did not provide evidence that the vessel hit in the Caribbean was ferrying drugs. A video posted on X showed an image of what appeared to be a moving boat followed by a flash.
Vice-President JD Vance has said on social media that "killing cartel members who poison our fellow citizens is the highest and best use of our military."
The U.S. has been beset for the past decade or so, as has Canada, with drug toxicity deaths that have largely been attributed to to the potency of fentanyl and similar opioids.

The Venezuelan gangs are more known to smuggle cocaine, though analysts say not in as large quantities as gangs or cartels from Colombia or Bolivia. It's also not clear if the attacked boats were transporting any product that was ultimately destined to arrive in the U.S., as opposed to Europe or Africa.

Gen. Francis Donovan, who leads the U.S. military's Southern Command, admitted in testimony to Congress in March that boat strikes "will be one of the main tools, and probably not the most effective" in limiting the illegal flow of drugs.

items: Why U.S. strikes on suspected drug boats have Canada ‘between a rock and a hard place’

blocks.text: The Washington Post reported in late July that a U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration assessment provided to lawmakers indicated that traffickers are both adapting their routes by sea to stay out of international waters, as well as diversifying by using more aircraft to transport drugs.

Mark Carney's government has generally avoided publicly criticizing the strikes unless pressed by reporters, though the Canadian military has said it has restricted intelligence to Operation Southern Spear, the U.S. campaign that has included targeting the boats.

articles.title: London Fashion Week 2026: The five trends we'll see in spring
articles.summary: As London Fashion Week comes to a close, here are the biggest trends for your wardrobe.

blocks.text: Image source, McQueen
Alexander McQueen made a historic return to London Fashion Week after 25 years, staging a homecoming show that fused severe tailoring with dark romanticism
ByAnnabel RackhamCulture reporter and Emma LynchPicture Editor
This London Fashion Week has been about return and renewal - as two of Britain's biggest designers showcased their spring/summer 2027 designs.

The first was Alexander McQueen, which as a brand moved to London after 25 years of showing in Paris - something Laura Weir, CEO of the British Fashion Council, told the BBC was "quite a big deal for us".
Creative director Seán McGirr brought the brand back to its roots, with a runway of devil horns, lace corsets and chainmail skull dresses.

Mulberry was the second designer to make its big return, this time after a nine-year absence, with Christopher Kane's debut collection centring around the brand's Baywater bag, while going big on leather in the form of coats, skirts and loafers.
Weir says the "big mission" for her and her team this season was to "re-platform London Fashion Week as not only a home for British design, but an engine for creativity and commercial growth".
Here are some of the major trends to come out of London Fashion Week 2026:
Messy girl aesthetic

blocks.caption: Image caption, Rejecting "quiet luxury" uniforms, Chopova Lowena, Sinead Gorey, and Conner Ives led London Fashion Week's embrace of the "messy girl" aesthetic by championing deliberate chaos, pairing intentionally undone tailoring and messy updos

blocks.text: Image source, Shutterstock/Gamma-Rapho via Getty Images

Rejecting "quiet luxury" uniforms, Chopova Lowena, Sinead Gorey, and Conner Ives led London Fashion Week's embrace of the "messy girl" aesthetic by championing deliberate chaos, pairing intentionally undone tailoring and messy updos
"The number one trend for this season is messy girl," says Elektra Kotsoni, deputy director for Vogue Business and Vogue Runway, whose team predicts the trends ahead of each season.
She tells the BBC: "We're going to be having a messy girl summer" and says "it's a reaction to the clean girl and quite luxury aesthetics that took over our Instagram feeds," last year.
Kotsoni says as "the world is quite messy" this form of dressing is a sign of "resilience" and rebellion.
She says if you are looking to replicate this trend, mix pastel colours, dreamy florals, and tactile materials to form "unexpected clashes" that "look really messy".
This form of what Kotsoni calls "crazy styling" was on display at London Fashion Week - with the noisy clashes at Chopova Lowena, Sinead Gorey and Conner Ives.
Gardening-core

blocks.caption: Image caption, Erdem, Yuhan Wang, and Bora Aksu channelled a "gardencore" vibe, trading quiet luxury for unpolished, allotment-ready chaos - pairing parkas and structured trench outerwear with kitchen-garden details

blocks.text: Image source, NOWFASHION via Shutterstock/Getty Images/Gamma-Rapho via Getty Images

Erdem, Yuhan Wang, and Bora Aksu channelled a "gardencore" vibe, trading quiet luxury for unpolished, allotment-ready chaos - pairing parkas and structured trench outerwear with kitchen-garden details
According to Kotsoni - gardening is officially cool in the fashion world.

A new twist on the cottage-core looks that emerged post-pandemic, instead of gingham, wicker bags and sourdough starters, it's all about looking like you're fresh from planting seeds or operating a lawnmower.
"There are lots of gardening appropriate silhouettes on the runways," she says, including aprons, waterproof materials and trench coats.
It started with Spanish fashion house Loewe launching a watering can-shaped handbag a couple of months ago and has now translated on the runway with Erdem, Yuhan Wang and Bora Aksu.

Kotsoni says "fashion is always a reflection of what's happening in the world" and likes how designers have been able to "take an interest like gardening and present it as something" tangible in a fashion show.
Modern goddess

blocks.caption: Image caption, Dujancourt's free-spirited aesthetic, organic draping, trailing ribbons, and delicately hitched slip skirts

blocks.text: Image source, Gamma-Rapho via Getty Images
Dujancourt's free-spirited aesthetic, organic draping, trailing ribbons, and delicately hitched slip skirts
Whilst some designers have been taking cues from the great outdoors - others have been inspired by film.
Another key trend identified by Kotsoni's team is the idea of the modern goddess - a take on the styles of Ancient Greece and a nod to Christopher Nolan's hit film The Odyssey this summer.
Kotsoni says the items to look out for are "draped garments, breezy materials and lots of bohemian and flowy silhouettes".
Pauline Dujancourt's London Fashion Week show epitomised this style - focusing on maximum volume and billowing fabrics.
Kotsoni says these looks are in opposition to how guests themselves have been dressing at this fashion week, suggesting a turning of the tide.
"Everybody has been dressed really minimalist in a specific quiet luxury way and I think people are tired of that," she notes.
Orange

blocks.caption: Image caption, Mulberry, Justin Cassin, Enny Atelier and Vin + Omi all featured orange in thier shows

blocks.text: Image source, Getty Images
Mulberry, Justin Cassin, Enny Atelier and Vin + Omi all featured orange in thier shows
Whether your preference is melon, tangerine, ginger or coral - orange appears to be the big colour trend for next year.

Kotsoni says she is hedging her bets on whether a shade of orange will be Pantone's colour of the year for 2027 as it has already been making its way into celebrity styling (it's not too late to replicate Kylie Jenner and Timothée Chalamet's matching neon outfits , externalat the Marty Supreme premiere for Halloween) and on the runway.
Mulberry, Justin Cassin, Enny Atelier and Vin + Omi all featured orange in their London shows and presentations over the last couple of days.
Ballet

blocks.caption: Image caption, A school sports hall is transformed into a ballet stage for Edeline Lee's latest collection which drew inspiration from the intense discipline, repetition, and physical toll of classical dance

blocks.text: Image source, Victor VIRGILE/Gamma-Rapho via Getty Images
A school sports hall is transformed into a ballet stage for Edeline Lee's latest collection which drew inspiration from the intense discipline, repetition, and physical toll of classical dance
Ever the fashion muse, Chalamet is once again at the centre of another trend for 2027 - ballet.
After he said "no one cares" about the discipline in May this year, Kotsoni says she "thinks it's interesting" that it's now being forged as a clear trend for next year.
Edeline Lee put on a striking show in London - complete with models taking to the runway en pointe in a transformed school sports hall.

"Ballet is very much in fashion," she says, noting that this month's Vogue Italia has La Scala's principle dancer Roberto Bolle on the cover, whilst Royal Ballet dancer Francesca Hayward has recently been modelling for Armani and Chanel.

"Ballet flats are massive and still will be [next year] and small silhouettes for shoes are going to be prevalent next season," Kotsoni adds - encouraging fans of the style to seek out items in charity and vintage shops if they want to replicate the look.

articles.title: Houthis move to seize strategic terrain after Trump calls off airstrikes at last minute
articles.summary:
US president reportedly changed his mind over Saudi Arabia’s pleas for assistance as bombs were being loaded

Houthi fighters are moving to seize strategic heights in Yemen that would cut the…

blocks.text: Houthi fighters are moving to seize strategic heights in Yemen that would cut the Red Sea coast off from areas held ​by Saudi-backed forces after Donald Trump called off US strikes on the group at the last minute, reportedly as bombs were being loaded on to aircraft.

Amid increasingly heavy fighting in Yemen, which has displaced tens of thousands of people in recent weeks, the New York Times reported on Monday that the US president had flip-flopped wildly in recent days after a call from Saudi Arabia for US strikes on the Houthis.

It comes amid the Houthis’ rapid advance on the ground with the group gaining control over much of Yemen’s Red Sea coast from Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces and advancing to areas adjacent to the crucial Bab al-Mandab strait, which Saudi Arabia has used as an alternative route for oil exports bypassing disruption in the ⁠strait of Hormuz.

In the call reported by the New York Times, Saudi Arabia’s crown prince, Mohammed bin Salman, implored Trump to step in to help halt the Houthi advance after weeks of such appeals. Trump, who had been resisting joining the Saudi war in Yemen, after the call then told the Pentagon to prepare for airstrikes against the Houthis before reversing course once again, the report said.

blocks.caption: A camp for people displaced by the fighting in Yemen, near the city of Aden. Photograph: Reuters

blocks.text: Trump has frequently given mixed signals to Riyadh, telling reporters during a visit to Ireland earlier this month that the Houthis “called us, and they don’t want to fight us”, adding that the group was “allowing ships to pass” the Bab al-Mandab strait and that the situation would “work out very well”.
He added that the Houthi problem was limited to “one country” an apparent reference to Saudi Arabia promising to “take care of fixing that”.

The UN says hostilities in Yemen have displaced at least 125,000 people since the start of September. Taiz city has received the largest number of displaced persons, taking in up to 86,000 Yemenis since the recent escalation began.
The rapid advance by the Iran-aligned group this ‌month has extended the wider Middle East conflict to a new theatre and further threatened global energy supplies.

Washington has so far rebuffed repeated pleas from Prince Mohammed to join the fight in Yemen with the Houthis claiming on Saturday they had fired on Riyadh, where columns of smoke were visible near the main airport.

blocks.caption: Flames and large plume of black smoke seen rising near Riyadh airport

blocks.text: The Yemeni president, ⁠Rashad al-Alimi, ⁠spoke with Trump on Sunday, requesting ‌support for his ‌UN-recognised government in its fight against the Houthis. Trump ⁠made no direct pledge ​of military ​support during ​the call, sources said.
Saudi Arabia has launched hundreds of strikes in recent days on Houthi positions in the strategic Kahboub mountains, according to the group, but making little impact on the ​advance of its fighters.

Fighting has centred on the outskirts of the remote Al-Wazi’iyah district in Taiz province and Ras al-Ara along the Indian Ocean coast, which separate the Red Sea coast from the city of Aden, where the government is based. The Houthis aim to secure the rear of their forces around the Bab al-Mandab strait by taking control of the mountains, which would also allow them to open new ‌fronts, according to ⁠sources who spoke to Reuters.
after newsletter promotion

The surge in fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis has created a new dilemma for Trump, under pressure to help defend Washington’s close Saudi allies but anxious not to further expand the deeply unpopular war he launched in February against Iran.
The US bombed the Houthis for two months in early 2025, but Trump called off those strikes after reaching a ceasefire with the group and has kept out of the conflict since.

Amid the broad failure of the US-Israeli war against Iran, and with the US midterm elections looming, the Trump administration’s priorities appear to be to secure at least some oil supplies through the strait of Hormuz, while avoiding a wider entanglement in Yemen.

That, however, invites longer term risks, not least the growing alienation of key US allies in the Gulf, including Saudi Arabia where Washington is increasingly seen as an unreliable ally, that could also undermine the so-called “security for oil” understanding where the US provides a defence umbrella for Gulf states in exchange for energy supplies.
Reuters contributed to this report

articles.title: SC highlights importance of ‘justice zones’
articles.summary: The Supreme Court yesterday emphasized the need to enhance inter-agency coordination among government bodies handling justice and law, as evidenced by its establishment of 13 out of 20 “justice…

blocks.text: September 22, 2026 | 12:00am
SC Associate Justice Maria Filomena Singh presented the high court’s accomplishments during yesterday’s Justice Sector Coordinating Council (JSCC) Summit in Manila.
Supreme Court Public Information Office / Released

MANILA, Philippines — The Supreme Court (SC) yesterday emphasized the need to enhance inter-agency coordination among government bodies handling justice and law, as evidenced by its establishment of 13 out of 20 “justice zones” across the country in the past five years.

The justice zones, she explained, would be “envisioned to be ‘local pockets of efficiency’” where “courts, prosecutors, law enforcers and other justice sector partners directly work and communicate with each other to address local justice problems and ensure delivery of justice real-time.”

She noted that two particular justice zones “show(ed) improved case disposition rates, jail congestion rates, faster processing time for parole and probation applications and increased number of preliminary investigation and inquest proceedings conducted and completed.”

She cited as examples the reduction of jail congestion at the Naga City jails “from a high of 300 percent… now down to 50 percent” through the Naga City Justice Zone, and the period for processing parole and probation applications in the Balanga City Justice Zone plunging “from around 200 days in 2021 to 60 days today.”
Singh described the statistics as “encouraging… because they tell us that coordination is not merely about meetings memoranda, circulars or a paper structure.”
“When coordination actually works, people directly experience its results and the delivery of justice is felt,” she said.

The JSCC, which turned 16 this year, is composed of the SC as lead convener, the Department of Justice and the Department of the Interior and Local Government that “work on cross-cutting issues affecting the justice system while at all times respecting and preserving the independence of the offices and agencies.”
The body also aims to “adopt a coordinated strategy to justice sector policymaking, planning and operations for a coherent and effective sectoral approach to the administration of justice.”

Singh also laid down the JSCC’s future plans, which include the development of the “victim-sensitive guidelines in the justice system,” aimed at “protecting the safety and privacy of victims, support their right to information and services, their recovery and rehabilitation and provide special safeguards for children and persons with disabilities.”

She also reported the high court is “done with the writing of the Manual and the Protocol for Handling Cases Involving Women in Conflict with the Law” that would address “gender-specific needs of women throughout the justice process, from investigation, apprehension and prosecution, trial, detention and eventual reintegration.”

articles.title: Government launches AI on eGovPH superapp
articles.summary: The government has rolled out new artificial intelligence capabilities to the eGovPH superapp, meant to automate government transactions at no cost to Filipinos, as well as provide a range of other…

blocks.text: September 22, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — The government has rolled out new artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities to the eGovPH superapp, meant to automate government transactions at no cost to Filipinos, as well as provide a range of other services, such as language translation.

During yesterday’s launch of eGovAI, Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) Secretary Henry Aguda said the agency’s own developers built the new features, powered by Google Gemini.
“We are bringing government services together in one digital platform and with the launch of eGovAI, we are taking another step forward,” he noted.
Within eGovAI is a virtual assistant called “Kuya A,” which offers 11 main services as of launch.
Among these is a conversational tool for government services queries, as well as real-time mapping to show users the closest tourism sites they can visit.
Further, farmers can leverage eGovAI to seek cropping assistance, as it can provide general information, such as soil quality as well as the best season for certain produce.
Soon, Aguda said the AI would be able to show the weather forecast per area.
A language translator is also incorporated, which can understand most, if not all, Philippine languages to bridge communication gaps.
The platform also features an image identifier, a document extractor, a speech maker, a coder/ programmer, a Health AI assistant, a Laws and Regulations assistant and an Identity AI assistant.

The eGovAI is free to use on eGovPH, eliminating the cost for Filipinos to subscribe to an AI tool for their automation needs. It also aligns with the DICT’s push for AI adoption, underscored by the launch of an AI roadmap two weeks ago.
Greater public access

In a speech read by Cabinet Secretary Benhur Abalos at yesterday’s event, President Marcos said every technology should serve public interest and every Filipino should benefit from the opportunities it provides.

“Let us give Filipinos greater access to the tools they need to learn, participate and prosper. And let us ensure that as technology moves forward, no Filipino is left behind in the opportunities it creates,” the President said.

“Always remember that technology should sharpen our judgment, not replace it. Let us use AI as a tool to make well-informed decisions without surrendering our own capacity to question, discern and decide,” he added.
Data privacy protected

Addressing data protection concerns surrounding emerging technologies, Aguda pledged that the DICT will uphold strict governance standards, data privacy and robust security safeguards as the government expands its AI integrations.

“As we move forward into the era of artificial intelligence, we must also ensure that progress remains responsible and inclusive,” he said. “Privacy and security must be protected, accessibility and accountability must remain part of the process and public trust must always be earned.”
Asia’s AI powerhouse
The Philippine AI+ Infrastructure Masterplan (PAIIM) makes a case to turn the Philippines into Southeast Asia’s AI powerhouse.
PAIIM outlines measures that seek to attract up to $34.4 billion in investments on AI infrastructure until 2033.
PAIIM also sets a target of raising data center capacity of 1.5 gigawatts by 2033, so that by then, AI processing time is reduced to below 20 milliseconds.
As a whole, PAIIM projects that the investments would fund the reskilling of at least 1.3 million Filipinos, making them ready for AI jobs. — Alexis Romero, Elijah Felice Rosales

According to Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla, feuding politicians filing cases against each other were wasting people’s time.
Citing an incident in San Pablo City in Laguna, Remulla recalled the mayor and vice mayor were placed under preventive suspension.

articles.title: Student cited for heroism during Cotabato shooting rampage
articles.summary: There might have been more casualties in the Banga, South Cotabato campus shooting rampage on Friday, if not for a brave student who fought the attacker barehanded and forced him out of their…

blocks.text: September 22, 2026 | 12:00am
The hero student who saved many classmates from the carnage on their Banga, South Cotabato, campus on Sept. 18, 2026 has been discharged from the hospital and is now recuperating at home.
Handout photo via Department of Social Welfare and Development 12

MANILA, Philippines — There might have been more casualties in the Banga, South Cotabato campus shooting rampage on Friday, if not for a brave student who fought the attacker barehanded and forced him out of their classroom despite suffering a gunshot wound in the arm.

Banga Mayor Albert Palencia and South Cotabato Gov. Reynaldo Tamayo Jr. separately told reporters yesterday that a courageous male student of Banga National High School destroyed the windows at the rear of a classroom after shutting its door, allowing his classmates to escape and run to safety while his right arm was bleeding profusely from the gunshot wound.
“He is a hero. He exemplified what we call courage under fire, ignoring his gunshot wound bleeding then,” Tamayo said.
The student was brought to a hospital by an emergency response team from the Banga local government unit and has since been discharged.
He is now recuperating at home and receiving essential relief support from Palencia’s office and the South Cotabato Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office.
Aside from the hero student, seven others were wounded while three people were killed in Friday’s incident at the BNHS campus, including the attacker, who shot himself in the head after the shooting.

The incident shook residents of the supposedly peaceful Banga town and prompted administrators of elementary, secondary and tertiary schools in Banga and nearby towns to suspend classes temporarily as authorities work to restore normalcy at the BNHS campus.
“The Banga local government unit will give the hero student a special award for his heroic act,” Palencia said.
Tamayo likewise announced that the provincial government would also recognize the student’s bravery through a special citation.

articles.title: ‘Sara briefed on sub judice rule’
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte has been briefed on the impeachment court’s sub judice rule restricting statements outside Senate proceedings, according to defense spokesman Michael Poa.

blocks.text: September 22, 2026 | 12:00am
In this photo uploaded on Facebook on March 2, 2026, Vice President Sara Duterte personally visits residents affected by Typhoon Basyang at Iligan City Public Plaza.
Vice President Sara Duterte via Facebook

MANILA, Philippines — Vice President Sara Duterte has been briefed on the impeachment court’s sub judice rule restricting statements outside Senate proceedings, according to defense spokesman Michael Poa.
“I will not deny that there have been discussions between myself and the Vice President on what I think is skirting sub judice, skirting contempt,” Poa told reporters yesterday.
Prosecutors have called on the court to also apply the rule to the Vice President.
“If there are things that she is uncertain if its sub judice or not, she consults us and we give our opinion. Usually, she values our opinion,” Poa said.
Duterte did not entertain impeachment-related questions during her visit to Banga, South Cotabato yesterday.
The Vice President had accused senators of being influenced or controlled by Malacañang, House prosecution spokesman Rep. Zia Alonto Adiong pointed out earlier.
“It is correct to be fair and that if there are violations on Rule 18 or the sub judice rule, we should all be covered by that, including the defense, including myself,” Poa said.
Duterte’s health
Meanwhile, in an interview in Banga, Duterte said she was pleased that judges of the International Criminal Court have seen her father’s current condition.
“You saw his advanced age and I hope that they will discuss the state of his health,” she said.

articles.title: DILG seeks to abolish access to nihilistic sites
articles.summary: Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla has called for a total ban on websites and online platforms that promote violence and hate following three deadly school shooting incidents in the country this year.

blocks.text: September 22, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla has called for a total ban on websites and online platforms that promote violence and hate following three deadly school shooting incidents in the country this year.

Together with Philippine National Police (PNP) chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr., Remulla visited yesterday Banga National High School in South Cotabato, where a 16-year-old Grade 9 student shot 10 of his schoolmates on Friday, killing three, including himself, and wounding eight using a handgun owned by his father, who is a Department of Education (DepEd) employee.
Citing a police investigation report, Remulla said the student had been exposed to the deep dark web and was suffering from depression.
A background check on the suspect also showed that he had many friends and was neither a bully nor bullied in school.
Two other school shooting incidents in Tacloban and Zamboanga were perpetrated by students who were hooked on violent online games.
“This is the dark side of the unlimited access to the internet and it is time that we act as a community,” Remulla said.
In response, the government asked the National Telecommunications Commission (NTC) to make such websites inaccessible not only to minors but also to adults.
The NTC has since blocked two websites showing real-world violence upon the request of the PNP Anti-Cybercrime Group.
“The NTC has already directed our ISPs (internet service providers) to block access to these websites,” Co said at a news briefing in Camp Crame in Quezon City.
PNP spokesman Col. Allen Rae Co did not identify the websites, which authorities said were being used by predators to groom minors to commit violence such as mass shootings.
Other violent websites and online platforms are also being considered for blocking.
VP blames government
Vice President Sara Duterte also visited Banga to meet victims of the shooting and express her condolences.
During her visit, she called on authorities to gather and process all information related to the Banga shooting and create a culture of security within schools.

“We can see that if a child feels that there is no safe space where he or she would be allowed to talk about his or her feelings and what is going through his or her mind, they will look elsewhere such as in the social media, or other groups that they could find in the Internet,” she said. “This reminds us that when a government prioritizes political consolidation over fundamental governance, the protection of children is inevitably compromised.”

“The Marcos administration has failed the victims and survivors of the South Cotabato tragedy. Countless more Filipino children remain at risk of becoming casualties of this government’s incompetence and neglect,” she added. “We deserve better leadership than this.”
Digital safety
The DepEd, for its part, proposed adding another layer of school security through a School Digital Safety Campaign.

DepEd Secretary Sonny Angara said the department had already implemented several physical security measures in schools but stressed that keeping children safe also requires addressing risks in their digital lives.

“Keeping our children safe today means understanding that their world extends beyond the classroom and into their phones, games, group chats and social media. We need to give children, parents and teachers the knowledge and tools to navigate these spaces safely,” Angara said.

The campaign will provide practical and age-appropriate guidance on safe chatting and online behavior, grooming and online child exploitation, cyberbullying and online harassment, privacy, scams and protecting personal information.

It will also cover responsible social media use, gaming and online safety, exposure to violent or harmful online content, healthy screen time and digital well-being, as well as warning signs, reporting, referral and what to do when something happens.
In line with this, the Senate yesterday passed a twin bill seeking to protect children in schools and online against sexual exploitation and nihilistic violent extremism.

One of the bills is the SAGIP Bata Act. Sen. Risa Hontiveros explained that the bill aims to address emerging threats, including online grooming and recruitment of children for serious violent activities and nihilistic violent extremism.

The Senate also approved Sen. Bam Aquino’s Comprehensive School Safety Act, which would require schools to establish localized safety plans, emergency protocols and measures for prevention, response and recovery, including psychosocial support.
“Schools should be a safe space where our children learn, develop their character, and build their dreams. It should not be a place of fear, harm, or violence,” Aquino said.
Both bills received 17 votes, with no objections or abstentions.
Mental health epidemic
Aside from digital safety, DepEd has also called for stronger mental health support for learners and closer school communities.

Speaking before more than 5,000 teachers at the Quezon Educators Research Convention in Lucena City on Sunday, Angara urged educators to look beyond academics and become more aware of the personal circumstances and struggles of their students.
“There is a mental health epidemic among our youth today. We must acknowledge it, understand it and look into the roots of it,” he said.

Citing the Sept. 18 shooting in Banga, Angara said the incident should serve as a wake-up call for the education sector as adolescents face emotional distress and growing exposure to social media and online communities.

Echoing Angara, Quezon Gov. Angelina Tan called for a holistic approach involving schools, families, health workers and local governments to identify mental health concerns among children before these develop into more serious problems.
She also stressed the need for teachers, parents and local officials to work together in recognizing changes in learners’ behavior and addressing their concerns early.
Other threats?
Two teenagers, meanwhile, posted threatening remarks on Facebook days after the deadly Banga shooting.
One was an 18-year-old student in Tupi, South Cotabato, who was arrested Sunday night for brandishing a handgun on Facebook.

The suspect, identified only as Ailaden, was apprehended in Barangay Poblacion at around 10:30 p.m. and is facing complaints for alarm and scandal in relation to Republic Act 10175, or the Cybercrime Prevention Act.
Student, 13, threatens violence
Meanwhile, a 13-year-old Grade 8 student in Lambayong, Sultan Kudarat, was rescued after making two Facebook posts threatening to shoot people at Kapingkong National High School.
The first post read, “We will be the ones to carry out the shooting incident at Kapingkong tomorrow, I will kill them all” and was accompanied by a photograph of a short firearm.
The student made a second post with a picture of a long firearm and threatened to kill everyone on campus.
Nartatez said the cases should remind people to use social media responsibly and avoid posting messages that could threaten public safety, particularly in schools and communities.
“Let this be a reminder that social media is not a place to make threats or create fear,” he said.

He also urged the public not to repost unverified threats and reminded parents, schools and communities to guide students on responsible online behavior. — Michelle Zoleta, Evelyn Macairan, John Unson, Marc Jayson Cayabyab

articles.title: 6 new Philippines hotels awarded Michelin Keys
articles.summary: Six new hotels in the Philippines have been awarded Michelin Keys for being among the most outstanding hotels in the world.

blocks.text: September 22, 2026 | 12:00am
MANILA, Philippines — Six new hotels in the Philippines have been awarded Michelin Keys for being among the most outstanding hotels in the world.

The prestigious hospitality recognition body named El Nido Resorts Lagen Island in Palawan and Raffles Makati as the first two Michelin Key hotels in the Philippines for their “exceptional stay” service.

“Situated in a forested cove framed by limestone cliffs and facing out onto the aquamarine-hued Bacuit Bay, Lagen Island offers four types of accommodations: water cottages on stilts, beachfront cottages, forest rooms and forest suites,” said the Michelin Guide.
It also cited the resort’s sustainability through its repeatedly awarded environmentally sound practices.
Raffles Makati was elevated to two-Michelin Keys for its more intimate and exclusive hotel services.
The guide features the hotel’s Writers Bar, which was described as a “stylish tribute” to famous writers who have stayed at Raffles in Singapore over the years.

Four hotels, including NUSTAR Hotel Cebu in Cebu City, Hotel Okura Manila in Pasay, El Nido Resorts Pangulasian Island in Palawan and Manami Resort in Sipalay City were given one Michelin Key distinctions for the “very special stay” it offers visitors.

NUSTAR Hotel Cebu was recognized for its oversized 223 rooms, with deep soaking tubs and floor-to-ceiling windows overlooking sea and skyline views. Hotel Okura was cited for its location within the retail and entertainment complex Newport World Resorts.
“El Nido Resorts Pangulasian Island’s villas stand alongside a half-mile-long white-sand beach, with views of the archipelago’s other islands dotting the horizon,” the guide said.
Manami Resort, the five-hectare and only luxury resort on the southwest coast of Negros Occidental, was recognized for its proximity to the Sulu Sea, with “18 villas woven into the terrain.”
The Department of Tourism said the Michelin Keys serve as an opportunity to promote the country as a destination for exceptional stays.
“Every recognition earned by our tourism stakeholders contributes to a stronger Philippine tourism brand,” Dita Angara-Mathay said.

articles.title: DOE admits no immediate solution to Visayas power crisis
articles.summary: House committee on energy chairman Jose Alvarez pressed the Department of Energy (DOE) for an immediate solution to the continuing power shortage in the Visayas, but said the agency has yet to…

blocks.text: September 22, 2026 | 12:00am

House energy committee chairman Rep. Jose Alvarez (3rd from left) pressed the Department of Energy for an immediate solution to the continuing power shortage in the Visayas, but said the agency has yet to present one.
STAR / File

MANILA, Philippines — House committee on energy chairman Jose Alvarez pressed the Department of Energy (DOE) for an immediate solution to the continuing power shortage in the Visayas, but said the agency has yet to present one.
Alvarez questioned the DOE on why the Visayas continues to experience Yellow and Red alerts despite the interconnected grid.
“Why can’t Mindanao plants supply? Why can’t Luzon supply?” Alvarez asked.

Energy Undersecretary Mario Marasigan explained that simultaneous outages of major power plants in Mindanao have limited the power that can be transferred to the Visayas. Only about 50 megawatts can currently be transferred because several plants remain unavailable.
Marasigan also acknowledged the Visayas’ lack of conventional and baseload generation, particularly in Negros.
“Negros has no baseload except for one geothermal. It’s all renewable – solar. There’s a lack of conventional plants,” Marasigan said.
He added that the intermittency of renewable energy can further tighten supply when generating units go offline.
Marasigan said the DOE’s focus is now on generation companies and the immediate return of unavailable plants.
What’s important is that the plants on outage are back, he said.

Despite these efforts, Marasigan warned that Yellow and Red alerts could still occur in the second and third weeks of October, underscoring the continuing vulnerability of the Visayas power supply. — Delon Porcalla

articles.title: DICT wants socmed sites to get congress franchise
articles.summary: Tech giants like Meta Platforms Inc. may soon need to secure a legislative franchise before they can offer digital platforms such as Facebook and Messenger to Filipinos.

blocks.text: September 22, 2026 | 12:00am

Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) Secretary Henry Aguda favors the imposition of stricter rules on the entry of online platforms in the country in the wake of tragic events believed to have been caused by their negligence.
Anadolu photo
MANILA, Philippines — Tech giants like Meta Platforms Inc. may soon need to secure a legislative franchise before they can offer digital platforms such as Facebook and Messenger to Filipinos.
Aguda, who had a dialogue with Meta representatives in August, said it’s time for regulators to treat digital channels like Facebook as broadcasting systems.

As such, he supports the passage of measures mandating digital outlets, particularly social media networks, to secure a congressional franchise. This way, Aguda said the government could force online platforms to fully comply with local laws.

Aguda said online sites like Facebook are facing growing scrutiny from several governments. In August, Meta agreed to pay up to $18 billion in the United States to cover civil cases over teenage addiction to Facebook and Instagram.
The settlement ended a federal trial against Meta’s products that allegedly resulted in social media addiction for children.
Apart from this, Poland is asking the European Commission to slap a $291-million fine on Meta, accusing the developer of failing to curb fraudulent ads on its social media networks.
In the Philippines, Aguda said Facebook is to be blamed for failing to block violent content seen as influential in the series of deadly school shootings in Tacloban, Zamboanga and South Cotabato.

Aguda favors the passage of measures like House Bill 4786 or the Social Media Platform Franchise Act. HB 4786 treats social media sites like Facebook as broadcasting channels, needing to secure a legislative franchise prior to operating here.
HB 4786 will also mandate digital platforms to establish a local office with a designated country representative. It will require the creation of a grievance redress system accessible to Filipinos.
For now, the DICT is waiting for Meta to sign a memorandum of understanding aimed at strengthening protection measures for the youth.
The memorandum outlines a series of measures that the Philippines wants Meta to comply with to improve content regulation and safety features for young Filipino users.

articles.title: US strikes on alleged drug boats may constitute ‘crimes against humanity’, UN finds
articles.summary:
Dozens of US attacks on boats in the Pacific and Caribbean have killed more than 230 people since September 2025

A special rapporteur for the UN human rights council has concluded that there…

blocks.text: A special rapporteur for the UN human rights council has concluded that there are “reasonable grounds to believe” that the United States attacks on boats allegedly carrying drugs in the Pacific and Caribbean “constituted crimes against humanity”.

The boat strikes, carried out since September 2025 on the stated grounds of stopping drugs being trafficked by sea to the US, have killed more than 230 people. The latest, on Saturday, killed four people in the Caribbean.

The UN itself, along with several human rights organisations, lawyers and international law experts, had already described the bombings as “extrajudicial killings”, but special rapporteur Ben Saul went further.

In a briefing note posted by Saul on social media on Sunday night and first reported by the BBC, Saul wrote that, in addition to “serial extrajudicial killings”, the attacks were “in violation of the right to life, being unjustified in national or personal self-defence or under international humanitarian law, the international law of the sea, narcotics suppression conventions, or international counter-terrorism law”.
He added: “There are reasonable grounds to believe that the reported 68 attacks that killed 223 people constituted crimes against humanity of murder under customary international law.”

The report cites 68 US attacks that killed 223 people. It is unclear how recently the figures were updated – tallies by organisations such as the Washington Office on Latin America put the death toll at 234 people in 66 attacks.

US Southern Command, which has coordinated the attacks, posted on Saturday, alongside a grainy video, that it had “executed a lethal, kinetic strike on a go-fast vessel operating along established narco-trafficking routes in the Caribbean. Confirmed intelligence revealed the vessel’s active involvement in narco-trafficking. The operation killed four narco-terrorists”.

As has become standard in announcements of such attacks, the US did not identify the victims or provide any details about the alleged intelligence that supposedly confirmed their involvement in drug trafficking.
Saul’s report rejects the claim made by Donald Trump before Congress that the strikes amounted to “self-defence” against “designated terrorist organizations”.
The special rapporteur wrote that the crews were not “militarily armed and possessed the intent and capacity to launch military attacks” against the US.

“Even assuming that the vessels and crew attacked were members of the criminal groups listed as terrorist, such organizations have not mounted any ‘armed attack’ on the United States so as to trigger a right of self-defence,” he added.
The US Department of State has not yet responded to a request for comment.

Although Trump recently claimed the bombings had stopped 97% of all illegal drugs entering the US by sea, according to available data, the attacks have had no impact on the volume of cocaine entering the US.

Journalists and human rights groups have managed to identify some of the victims, who in many cases were innocent or, when suspected of involvement in criminal activity, were at best low-ranked participants in trafficking networks.

articles.title: China ship's ramming of BFAR vessel 'unacceptable breach of int'l law' --Teodoro
articles.summary: Defense Sec. Gilberto Teodoro Jr. denounced a China Coast Guard vessel"s ramming of a BFAR ship in the West Philippine Sea as a breach of international law that the Philippines cannot ignore.

blocks.text: Published September 21, 2026 11:47pm

Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. denounced a China Coast Guard (CCG) vessel’s ramming of a Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR) ship in the West Philippine Sea as a breach of international law that the Philippines cannot ignore.
In a “24 Oras” report by Chino Gaston on Monday, the Defense Chief noted that the offense could have even been classified as a "criminal act" had anyone been injured in the incident.

“Kung may nasaktan doon, that’s a criminal act na ginawa nila eh [Had anyone been hurt, what they did would be considered a criminal act]. It’s not merely a violation of maritime rules and regulations but a criminal act by the Chinese Coast Guard,” Teodoro said.
He added that the defense department will not take such a violation of international law lightly.
“We will be addressing that. I’m not going to talk about specifics now pero [but], definitely, our personnel are already developing options for addressing this,” Teodoro added.
The incident occurred last Friday, September 18, near Abad Santos Shoal—located 54 nautical miles off Palawan and well within the country’s 200-nautical-mile exclusive economic zone (EEZ).
Reports indicated that the crew of the BFAR vessel BRP Datu Magat Salamat grew alarmed as CCG vessel 21585 slowly approached.
In Gaston’s report, the Chinese vessel reportedly crisscrossed behind the BFAR ship before ultimately sideswiping its stern.
While no BFAR crew members were injured, the ship sustained severe damage.

The government’s security cluster is reportedly drafting a response plan to present to President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. regarding China’s aggressive maneuvers, which appear to be moving closer to the Philippines.
Teodoro stated that this is a pressing challenge the country must address immediately.
“Bagong hamon ito dahil mas malapit sa atin at kailangan addressin din talaga natin nang mas mabilis,” Teodoro said.
(This is a new challenge because it occurred closer to home, and we really need to respond faster.)

“‘Yung sasabihin natin na we will always play the victim—we are not playing the victim, but we are just bringing facts to light na dati hindi lalabas ‘yan [at] ngayon nilalabas natin. At aminado naman tayo [na] napakatagal na panahong pinabayaan natin itong capabilities,” he added.

(Some say we always play the victim—we are not playing the victim, but simply bringing facts to light that were previously kept hidden. And we admit that we neglected these capabilities for a very long time.)
For his part, US Ambassador to the Philippines Lee Lipton condemned the incident, describing it as a “deliberate ramming” by the CCG.
“We commend the sustained professionalism of our Philippine Allies in the face of this dangerous, destabilizing act,” Lipton said in a statement on X.
In response, the Chinese Embassy rejected Lipton’s statement, calling it an attempt to incite and encourage the Philippines to intrude and cause trouble at sea.

The Chinese Embassy also claimed that the BFAR vessel ignored warnings from the CCG, alleging that it intentionally altered its course and crossed in front of the Chinese ship, which ultimately led to the collision.
In another development on Monday, Teodoro opened the ASEAN Defense Ministers' Meeting-Plus at the Subic Bay Freeport Zone in Zambales.
The event brought together navies from ASEAN nations and key allies, including the US, the UK, Australia, and Japan.

The Chinese delegation did not attend the meeting, which featured joint cooperative activities among warships in the waters near Bajo de Masinloc—an area China occupies and claims despite falling inside the Philippines' EEZ. — Lyjah Tiffany Bonzo/BM, GMA News

articles.title: Senate OKs bills protecting children vs online abuse, school violence
articles.summary: Two key bills promoting the protection of children from online abuse, exploitation and ensuring safer school environments have been passed on third and final reading by the Senate on Monday.

blocks.text: Published September 21, 2026 11:44pm
Two key bills promoting the protection of children from online abuse, exploitation and ensuring safer school environments have been passed on third and final reading by the Senate on Monday.
During session, the Comprehensive School Safety Act and the SAGIP BATA Act were approved after both measures received 17 affirmative votes, with zero negative votes and no abstentions.
Senate Bill No. 2426 or the Comprehensive School Safety Act, seeks to institutionalize a framework for preventing, responding to, and recovering from violence and other safety threats in schools.
The measure was passed following several fatal school shooting incidents across the country, the most recent occurring just three days ago in Banga, South Cotabato.
Senator Bam Aquino, the principal sponsor and a co-author of the bill, previously explained that the proposed framework is structured around three main pillars: prevention, response, and recovery.

Senator Raffy Tulfo, who supported the bill, highlighted several key provisions, including the installation of CCTV cameras in classrooms and common areas, as well as the provision of counseling and psychological support in coordination with the Department of Health.
“I firmly believe that none of us deserve to learn and teach in fear,” Tulfo said.

Senator Robin Padilla, who likewise supported the school safety measure, shared his views on school violence in the country, pointing out that recent school shooting incidents are “not part of Asian culture.”
“Hindi po kultura ng Asyano ang pumunta sa isang paaralan at mamaril. Hindi lang mamaril ah—manalsal pa po yung iba. Ito po ay kultura ng ibang nasyon [at] ibang lahi,” Padilla said.
(It is not in Asian culture to go to a school and shoot people. Not just shoot—some even commit acts of violence. This is a culture from other nations and other races.)
SAGIP BATA Act

The upper chamber also approved on Monday SB No. 1819 or the Safeguarding Against Grooming, Inducement and Predation, and Building Accountability for Technology-Facilitated Abuse or Exploitation (SAGIP BATA) Act.

Once signed into law, the measure will replace Republic Act No. 11930 or the Anti-Online Sexual Abuse or Exploitation of Children (OSAEC) and the Anti-Child Sexual Abuse or Exploitation Materials (CSAEM) Act.
It establishes a stronger preventive framework to protect children from grooming, exploitation, and manipulation across both physical and digital platforms.

The bill aims to bolster child protection safeguards, regulatory protocols, and enforcement mechanisms to combat technology-facilitated sexual abuse, the proliferation of child sexual abuse material, and the orchestration of serious violent crimes against minors.
It also addresses emerging threats, including the use of artificial intelligence to generate sexualized content or exploit children.

Senator Francis “Kiko” Pangilinan, who voted in favor of the measure, underscored the specific acts the law criminalizes that include grooming, luring, child sexual extortion, image-based sexual abuse, sexualization of children, livestreaming, and the creation and distribution of CSAEM.
“Kinilala ng panukala na hindi kinakailangang magkaroon ng pisikal na contact ang isang salarin para lubhang mapinsala ang isang bata,” Pangilinan said.
(The measure recognizes that a perpetrator does not need physical contact to inflict grave harm on a child.)
The measure, as Pangilinan cited, also holds tech companies and private businesses operating in the digital sphere accountable.

SAGIP BATA Act mandates that online platforms, internet intermediaries, payment service providers, and virtual asset providers implement strict safety protocols, including age verification systems. — BAP, GMA News

Presley Gerber, the son of supermodel Cindy Crawford, died on Sunday at age 27, a family representative said.

Gerber, a model and mental health advocate, died at a rehab facility in Los Angeles, according to online records of the L.A. County Medical Examiner. No cause of death or further details have been shared at this time.
The death was confirmed by Allie Jenkins, a representative for Crawford and her husband Rande Gerber.

In December 2025, Gerber discussed taking several medications, including buprenorphine, Xanax and Valium, while dealing with panic attacks in a since-deleted Instagram video, according to People Magazine.
In August, his sister Kaia ⁠Gerber spoke about her brother's struggles ​in an ⁠interview with Vogue magazine. "When something like that happens in a family, it kind of levels everyone," she said.

articles.title: No avoiding the cost of inaction on climate, Anthony Albanese says in New York
articles.summary:
Ahead of United Nations meeting, prime minister says Australians knows the impact of global heating as well as anyone

Australia understands the dangers of global warming and the urgency of…

blocks.text: Australia understands the dangers of global warming and the urgency of climate action as much as any other country, Anthony Albanese has said in a keynote speech ahead of the United Nations general assembly.

Speaking at the opening of the Climate Week event at the United Nations in New York on Monday, the prime minister said Australians had experienced the impact of climate change up close with a series of disastrous bushfires and floods in the past decades.
People had faced up to the adversity, he said, but now it was the turn of politicians to match their “bravery” and take the strong action needed to try to tackle the problem.
“We need to come together, to meet the problem head on,” he told the assembly.
“There’s no avoiding the scale of our responsibility – or the cost of inaction.”
Australia understood the important role it must play and the need to back ”something positive” and to move forward and “build a better future for the next generation”.

His government had set an “ambitious but achievable” target to reduce emissions by 62- 70% on 2005 levels by 2035 and, with a mixture of renewable power backed by gas, Australia “will get there” he said.
“We are now a leader in home battery installation, with Australians installing ten thousand batteries each week – more than half a million in the past year.”
He said Australia was also helping Pacific countries hard-hit by the climate crisis including A$100m towards the Pacific Resilience Facility.

In addition, the Australian government’s REnew Pacific Program was going towards climate resilient classrooms in Vanuatu and Fiji, to clean energy and water on one of Kiribati’s most remote islands. He claimed the program has “directly improved 300,000 lives”.

articles.title: Inquest into British aid workers killed in Gaza may call on Israeli and UK military chiefs
articles.summary:
Lawyer tells review hearing that families wish to know whether weaponry involved in the deaths was made in UK

Israeli and UK military commanders could be requested to give evidence to an…

blocks.text: Israeli and UK military commanders could be requested to give evidence to an inquest concerning three British workers killed in Gaza when aid vehicles they were travelling in were hit by an airstrike.
It is also possible that the inquest into the deaths of John Chapman, 57, Jim Henderson, 33, and James Kirby, 47, may examine whether the weaponry that killed the men was made in the UK.

Until now, the focus of the inquest has been on the role played by the aid organisation in charge of the convoy and the security firm that was protecting it. But at a pre-inquest review, Maria Voisin, the senior coroner for Avon, indicated that the scope of the final hearing would probably be widened to include the role of Israeli authorities in the deaths.

The coroner said she was “minded” to designate the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) and the colonel who ordered the strikes, Nochi Mendel, as “interested parties” for the inquest. Interested parties are often relatives of the person who died or an organisation or individual believed to be closely involved in what happened.
Israeli military authorities last month said they would not open criminal investigations into the strike, a move the UK, Australian and Canadian governments called “shameful”.

In a written submission to the court, Pete Weatherby KC, for Henderson, compared the case to that of the novichok attack by the Russian state in Salisbury, in which the British woman Dawn Sturgess was killed.

In that case, the high court in London ruled the lack of any criminal investigation by the Russian authorities and the strong public concern surrounding the circumstances of Sturgess’ death necessitated the expansion of the scope of the investigation.

Lawyers for the three men accepted that it was possible Israel would not cooperate with the inquest but called for UK ministers to try to apply pressure if needed. Another element the families are keen to have investigated is the role the British military may have played in the incident in April 2024.

Weatherby’s submission says that a Royal Air Force surveillance plane spent about five hours above Gaza on the day of the attack, seemingly returning to base minutes before the airstrikes were launched. The families want to know what, if any, surveillance the plane gathered about the convoy – and what was shared with the Israeli authorities.

The barrister also told the review hearing in Flax Bourton, near Bristol, it was a “matter of public concern” and “great importance to the family” to find out if the weaponry that killed the men was made in the UK.
Voisin said she was open minded about which issues the inquest would consider and would keep some under review. “It’s very much a case of throwing the net wide at the moment,” she said.

In a statement, Henderson’s father, Neil Henderson, said: “We hope the coroner will carry out a thorough investigation into the attack that killed Jim and the others [including] an exploration of all the issues relevant to his death, encompassing the decisions and policies leading to the attack, and what role, if any, UK authorities or military equipment originating from the UK may have played.”
A further pre-inquest review will take place in March. No date for the final hearing has been set.

articles.title: More than 150,000 underwater explosives used to deter seals at Tasmanian salmon farms since 2016
articles.summary:
Salmon companies operating in Tasmanian marine areas deployed almost 1,800 explosives in first half of 2026, government figures reveal

  • Get our

blocks.text: More than 150,000 underwater explosives have been used to deter seals at Tasmanian salmon farms since 2016, according to new government data.

Department of Natural Resources and Environment (NRE Tas) data released last week revealed salmon companies directed almost 1,800 underwater explosives at seals at fish farms in the first half of 2026.
Since the start of 2016, the three salmon companies operating in Tasmanian marine areas – Huon Aquaculture, Tassal and Petuna – have deployed 150,488 underwater explosives.

Four fur seals died in the first half of 2026 – two at Tassal leases and two at Huon Aquaculture sites. Two died entangled at salmon cages, one from a boat strike and another in an attempt to sedate and relocate an animal. Since the start of 2021, 48 seals have died at Tasmanian salmon farms.

The use of underwater explosives against seals has declined sharply since April 2021, possibly in response to the publication of Richard Flanagan’s book Toxic. Since early 2022, NRE Tas has released biannual data, with a company-by-company and month-by-month breakdown of the use of devices against seals, after a right-to-information request by the Tasmanian Inquirer.

Huon Aquaculture, owned by the Brazilian meat company JBS, accounted for 1,126 of the explosives used in the first half of 2026, almost two-thirds of the total. Of these, 892 were used at the company’s leases in Storm Bay off the coast of Bruny Island, with the remainder at sites in the D’Entrecasteaux Channel and Huon River.

Huon is now the largest salmon producer in the state, according to an analysis of government production data published by SalmonBusiness. After rotting salmon flesh washed up on beaches in the D’Entrecasteaux Channel in early 2025, and incidents of mass deaths at fish farms over the past two years, the company launched a PR blitz, including a video featuring seals swimming in the ocean.
Tassal’s 2025 sustainability report said the company aimed to “phase out” the use of seal deterrents, but did not specify a deadline.
after newsletter promotion

Huon was asked whether it had a policy to phase out deterrents, and whether the high level of underwater explosive use against seals at the Storm Bay leases indicated the cages there were more prone to breakage due to exposure to rougher conditions.

The company did not respond to these specific questions, but a Huon spokesperson said the company took its responsibility to protect wildlife seriously and was evaluating initiatives to improve wildlife safety. “This includes upgrades to existing infrastructure, adoption of new technologies to deter wildlife, and engagement with specialist consultants to assess and reduce interaction risks,” the spokesperson said.

In its sustainability report, Tassal reported that seals gained access to salmon cages 1,100 times in the past three years. It said there was a 26% fall in seals getting into cages in 2025 compared with the previous year.

But the company’s use of explosives against seals has begun rising again after four years of decline. In the first half of 2026, it used 551 explosive devices, more than double the number in the same period in either of the two preceding years. More than half of these devices were used at leases on the Tasman Peninsula.

Tassal also used 31 bean bag rounds – fabric-coated plastic shells containing lead shot – against seals at its leases on the Tasman Peninsula. Tassal is the only salmon company that uses these devices in Tasmania.

Tassal was asked whether its increased use of explosives at its Tasman Peninsula leases was due to the seal population near Nubeena growing, and whether the company had an end date for using devices against seals. Tassal, which is owned by Canadian multinational Cooke Aquaculture, did not respond.
Petuna, the smallest of the state’s three marine salmon producers, used 82 underwater explosives against seals at leases in Macquarie Harbour and 38 at leases in the Tamar River.
